question: A charged particle moves in a uniform magnetic field. Explain why the magnetic force is always perpendicular to the velocity of the particle. Hence show that the magnetic force does no work on the particle. A charge of $4.0\times10^{-6}\text{ C}$ moves with speed $2.0\times10^5\text{ m s}^{-1}$ perpendicular to a magnetic field of $0.30\text{ T}$. Calculate the force acting on it.

options.A: Magnetic force is parallel to velocity, so it does positive work; $F=qvB=0.24\,\text{N}$.
options.B: The magnetic force is perpendicular to $\vec B$ only, so it changes kinetic energy; $F=0.12\,\text{N}$.
options.C: $\vec F=q(\vec B\times\vec v)$ is along displacement; therefore, $W\ne0$ and $F=0.48\,\text{N}$.
options.D: $\vec F=q(\vec v\times\vec B)$ is perpendicular to velocity and displacement. Hence $W=\int\vec F\cdot d\vec r=0$, so speed and kinetic energy do not change. For perpendicular motion, $F=qvB=(4.0\times10^{-6})(2.0\times10^5)(0.30)=0.24\,\text{N}$.
